kyoto.name: Kyoto Station 京都駅
kyoto.intro: Better news than you'd expect — but mind the clock: the fast wins are konbini rice + omiyage near the gates; the sit-down GF/vegan gems (even a gluten-free vegan ramen) are up on the restaurant floors and need a transfer with time to spare.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: On a short connection, don't climb to the restaurant floors — these are fast and close to the tracks.
sections.where: Konbini & kiosks on the concourse; JR Isetan B2 depachika (a bit further); omiyage shops by the Central Gate.

rows.t: Konbini: plain salt onigiri, boiled egg, edamame, fruit
rows.note: the universal celiac/vegan train move — read labels; plain salt onigiri is safest
rice/bean based, allergen-labeled; see Omiyage below

rows.t: JR Isetan B2 depachika veg/salad packs
rows.note: undressed vegetable packs; check dressing/dashi

sections.tip: Under ~15 min to change trains: konbini salt-onigiri + edamame + a yatsuhashi from the nearest omiyage stand, and eat on board.

sections.verdict: Real in-station GF/vegan exists — anchored by UNO RAMEN, a dedicated GF+vegan shop; two more vegan-friendly spots were missed by Vegewel; celiacs should still confirm on-site.
sections.where: Kyoto Ramen Koji (10F), JR Isetan 'Eat Paradise' (11F), Porta underground (B1, closer/faster).

rows.note: Dedicated GF+vegan — rice/kombu noodles, GF soy, soymilk broth; kitchen bans gluten & animal products (own site + HappyCow + FindMeGlutenFree); brand-new Dec 2025 so confirm on-site.
Vegan veg/kombu-broth ramen bowl (HappyCow + MATCHA), but wheat noodles + shared fish/meat kitchen — not GF; confirm the veg broth as some variants use bonito-kelp.
Two plant-based donburi confirmed no animal products (Hachidory/Vegewel), but likely wheat soy sauce so GF is ask — confirm on-site.
Own menu shows fish dashi + wheat throughout; vegan set only ‘on advance request’ (Vegewel flags info unverified) — call ahead; not the Kitano flagship.
Udon = wheat; soba usually wheat-blended and broth is kombu + katsuobushi (bonito) dashi — a celiac and vegan trap (kyotostation.com + Tabelog).

sections.tip: For a celiac OR vegan with time, UNO RAMEN is the move — a genuinely GF + vegan ramen inside the station.

sections.verdict: No certified-gluten-free and no truly vegan ekiben here. Almost everything is soy-glazed, fried, or fish/meat/egg based.
sections.where: Inside Shinkansen gates: Grand Kiosk, Delica Station, Maiko, Koto Miyabi (~6:30–21:30). Outside: Ekiben Nigiwai Kyoto (~7:00).

wheat batter + soy
sweet soy, dashi, egg

sections.tip: If you must grab a bento, vinegar-cured saba-zushi is the least-bad GF gamble — read the label; nothing here is celiac-safe.

sections.verdict: Packaged = allergen-labeled, so you can verify 小麦 (wheat). And Kyoto's #1 souvenir, yatsuhashi, is rice-based — a real GF/vegan win.
sections.where: The CUBE (Omiyage Koji Kyomachi 1F; 2F Omiyage Kaidō, Nishitoshi pickles, Ogura wagashi), Omiyage Kaidō (Porta), Kyoto Porta, JR Isetan depachika. ~6:00–23:45.

rows.note: rice flour + sugar + cinnamon; most anko/nikki are vegan. Wheat-free recipe BUT shared-wheat facilities (cross-contamination) — fine for gluten-avoiders, celiacs weigh that line. Aoyama Mameju is labeled vegan+GF; Nishio & Shōgoin run 米粉 lines.

sections.tip: Hero buy: nama-yatsuhashi (anko/nikki) — vegan and rice-based, grabbable in seconds.

playbook.tight: Under ~15 min to change trains: konbini plain salt onigiri (塩むすび) + edamame + a yatsuhashi from the nearest omiyage stand — all near the gates, eat on board.
playbook.gf: Real meal with time: UNO RAMEN (GF+vegan, 10F). Quick: konbini salt onigiri, boiled egg, edamame, fruit + omiyage rice-flour yatsuhashi/yokan. Skip ekiben. Nearest DEDICATED GF bento is Michinori in Nagoya.
playbook.vegan: Real meal with time: UNO RAMEN (10F) or Kyo-Tofu Fujino (11F). Quick: Isetan B2 veg packs + konbini salt onigiri & edamame + omiyage (yatsuhashi, yokan). Off-station: Gen, Hachidori Table. Always ask 'dashi wa sakana?'

hiroshima.name: Hiroshima Station 広島駅
hiroshima.intro: Hiroshima Station is a busy Shinkansen-to-tram hub with the large ekie complex attached, but it has no verified dedicated GF or vegan sit-down restaurant inside the gates — for a tight celiac/vegan transfer your safest bets are konbini staples and a few carefully-chosen omiyage. Read every label: wheat soy sauce and bonito dashi hide in almost all the local specialities.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Doable — the Seven-Eleven Heart-in is inside the gates (Shinkansen and local-line sides), so plain rice, fruit and soymilk are minutes away; assemble your own meal rather than trusting prepared items.
sections.where: Seven-Eleven Heart-in inside the ticket gates (2F, across from the central gate, and on the local-line side); konbini and depachika in ekie 1F just outside the gates.

rows.t: Shio-musubi 塩むすび (plain salt rice ball)
rows.note: Plain salt and rice is the simplest pick; avoid filled onigiri — most use wheat-containing soy sauce or bonito, so confirm it is salt-only.
Pickled-plum rice is usually plant-based, but seasoning/shiso mixes vary and some add dashi — check the label.
Whole or pre-cut fruit is the most reliable GF and vegan grab; pure fruit with no syrup or seasoning.
Plain roasted unsalted nuts are fine; flavoured or coated nuts can carry wheat or soy seasoning, so check.
Adjusted (調整) versions add flavourings; the unsweetened 無調整 carton is plain soybeans and water.
Vegan-certified flavours exist, but the bars contain wheat-based ingredients — vegan yes, not GF.

sections.tip: Build a tray from single-ingredient items (rice, fruit, nuts, soymilk) instead of relying on a labelled bento — it is the fastest safe option when the clock is tight.

sections.verdict: No verified GF/vegan WALK-IN sit-down inside ekie — but Vegewel missed OKOSTA, an in-ekie okonomiyaki cooking experience with genuine gluten-free and vegetarian courses (reservation-only class, not a restaurant).
sections.where: ekie 6F restaurant floor and ekie 1F dining are mostly conventional Japanese eateries; for verified vegan dining you must leave the station.

rows.t: OKOSTA オコスタ (in ekie, near Shinkansen exit)
rows.note: GF course uses rice-flour noodles + GF-compatible sauce; a vegetarian course exists but batter has egg & dashi may be used; shared teppan with wheat okonomiyaki, no published cross-contamination protocol — celiacs treat as ask (Otafuku own site + gurutabi + dive-hiroshima + Food Diversity).
Standard Hiroshima okonomiyaki = wheat batter + wheat noodles + gluten sauce + bonito/pork dashi + shared griddle — no GF/vegan menu found.
Wheat noodles + pork/wheat-soy broth.
Farm-to-table local produce but no published GF/vegan menu — would have to ask on-site.
Genuine vegan + GF menus but NOT in-station — ~1.5–2 km near Hatchobori despite Vegewel filing it under ‘Hiroshima Station’; confirm hours (closed Mon/Tue).

sections.tip: If you have a real layover, eat before you reach the gates or pre-book an off-station vegan cafe — do not count on an in-station dedicated GF/vegan kitchen, because none is confirmed.

sections.verdict: Hiroshima's famous ekiben are built on the exact traps a celiac/vegan must avoid — anago (eel) and oyster bento use wheat soy sauce, sweet tare and bonito, and are animal-based. Treat them as a no by default.
sections.where: Ekiben counters on the Shinkansen concourse and in ekie (Hiroshima Ekiben Co. lineup).

rows.note: Eel is not vegan, and the rice/tare is cooked with wheat-containing soy sauce — not GF either.
Seasonal oyster bento — oysters are not vegan, and rice cooked in oyster stock plus fried oysters (wheat batter) and soy seasoning rule out GF.
All-oyster bento with fried oyster (wheat batter) and yuzu-miso; shellfish and wheat — avoid.
A plain-rice bento is the only conceivable fallback, but garnishes, pickles and furikake often carry soy/dashi — inspect every component.

sections.tip: Hiroshima ekiben are essentially off-limits for strict GF/vegan; default to a konbini shio-musubi plus fruit instead of risking the speciality bento.

sections.verdict: The big win is Nishikido (にしき堂, ekie 2F): its rice-flour nama-momiji is wheat-free, and its Momiji Manju Light is made with no wheat, egg or dairy — but both are made in a shared wheat facility, so it is 'ask' for strict celiacs. Setouchi lemon condiments are the cleanest GF+vegan gifts.
sections.where: Nishikido 1-gō-ten, ekie 2F (approx 8:00–21:00); ekie omiyage zone; Setouchi/Hiroshima brand counters.

rows.note: Mochi/rice-flour skin with no wheat in the recipe, but it contains egg and is made on shared wheat lines — not vegan (egg), GF only if cross-contamination is acceptable, so ask.

rows.t: Momiji Manju Light もみじ饅頭Light (Nishikido)
rows.note: Made free of the 7 major allergens (no wheat, egg or dairy — uses rice flour and soymilk), so vegan-friendly; but the factory also handles wheat/egg/dairy, so end GF on ask for celiacs.
Standard momiji-manju and Setouchi lemon cakes use a wheat-flour sponge, plus egg/dairy — avoid on both counts.
Lemon juice, salted chilli, brewed vinegar, salt and lemon peel — no allergens listed and plant-based; a reliable GF+vegan Hiroshima gift.
Additive-free lemon syrups (lemon + beet sugar) are GF and vegan, but some candies/jams add gelatin or honey — check each product.
Hiroshima oyster gifts are shellfish-based (not vegan) and oyster sauce/seasonings typically include wheat — skip.

sections.tip: Go straight to Nishikido on ekie 2F for the rice-flour momiji items, and grab a bottle of Lemoscco — between them you cover a memorable GF/vegan Hiroshima gift, just flag the shared-facility caveat to a strict celiac.

playbook.tight: Hit the Seven-Eleven Heart-in inside the gates and build a meal from shio-musubi, whole fruit, plain nuts and unsweetened soymilk — fastest reliable option with no kitchen to quiz.
playbook.gf: Assume every Hiroshima speciality (okonomiyaki, ramen, anago/oyster ekiben) carries wheat soy sauce, bonito dashi or wheat batter; lean on plain rice, fruit and Lemoscco, and treat Nishikido's rice-flour momiji as 'ask' because of shared wheat lines.
playbook.vegan: Watch for hidden bonito dashi in 'vegetable' dishes and onigiri seasonings; eel and oysters are never vegan; safe vegan picks are plain rice, fruit, unsweetened soymilk, Lemoscco and Nishikido Momiji Manju Light, with off-station Vegewel cafes for a proper sit-down meal.

kanazawa.name: Kanazawa Station 金沢駅
kanazawa.intro: Kanazawa is a seafood-and-wagashi town, so the station leans fish-heavy (nodoguro, crab) and wheat-rich (Kaga fu, kintsuba) — plan around the clock. If your transfer is tight, grab konbini staples by the gates; with time to spare, the Hyakubangai shops reward a slower look.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Konbini are your reliable fallback: there is a Seven-Eleven Kiosk on the Shinkansen platform mezzanine (inside the gates) plus larger Heart-in stores around the concourse. Nothing is celiac-certified, so read labels and treat everything as cross-contamination risk.
sections.where: Seven-Eleven Kiosk JR Kanazawa platform mezzanine (inside gates); Seven-Eleven Heart-in by the concourse; Hyakubangai food halls.

rows.note: Plainest rice balls are the safest bet; skip fillings with mayo, tuna, or soy-seasoned mix — and ask, as seasonings can hide wheat.
Whole or pre-cut fruit is the no-think option when in doubt.
Seasonal konbini staple; just sweet potato, naturally GF and vegan.
Plain veg is fine but bagged dressings often use wheat soy sauce; take it undressed or check the packet — ask.
Unseasoned nuts and salted edamame travel well; avoid soy-glazed snack mixes.

sections.tip: Carry your own GF tamari/snacks — the station has no celiac-certified hot food, so build a meal from naturally GF konbini parts rather than relying on a single product.

sections.verdict: Verified GF/vegan sit-down INSIDE the station is essentially nil — the official Hyakubangai directory shows no dedicated GF or vegan restaurant; Onyasai shabu-shabu is the only realistically negotiable ‘ask’ fallback.
sections.where: Kanazawa Hyakubangai あんと / あんと西 restaurant zone (connected to the gates); Ume no Hana (reserve ahead).

rows.note: Customizable veg/tofu plates make it the best in-station fallback, but ponzu/sesame sauces & broths often carry wheat soy + bonito dashi — confirm broth and sauces.

rows.t: Ume no Hana 梅の花 (tofu/yuba kaiseki) — NOT in-station
rows.note: Vegan-on-reservation is real (own site), but it is NOT in-station — own site + Tabelog place it ~2.4 km / 8-min drive away; Vegewel’s ‘station’ tag is proximity only.
Whole concept is 麩 (wheat gluten) — not GF; confirmed via Fumuroya’s own site + Hyakubangai listing.
Veg ramen is veg-forward but allergen label confirms 小麦 (wheat noodles) and broth typically has pork/chicken/dashi — not GF, not reliably vegan.
Kanazawa curry roux is wheat-flour-thickened (allergen label confirms 小麦) over a meat/lard base — a celiac and vegan trap.

sections.tip: If you have a fixed Kanazawa stop, reserve Ume no Hana a day ahead and state celiac + vegan clearly; for a transfer, a sushi counter with your own GF tamari is the most flexible option.

sections.verdict: Kanazawa ekiben are a seafood showcase (nodoguro, snow crab, Noto beef) sold by historic makers like Takano Shoten, Daimaruya/Otomorou and Funayoshi — delicious but built on wheat soy sauce, mirin and bonito dashi. None are celiac-safe; vegans will struggle as nearly all are fish or meat.
sections.where: Ekiben stands inside the gates and in Hyakubangai あんと.

rows.note: Fish simmered/grilled in soy-mirin seasoning over dashi rice — wheat soy sauce and bonito throughout.
Crab itself is GF but vinegared rice and accompanying soy sauce usually contain wheat — ask, and it is never vegan.
Sampler box leans on soy-mirin glazes and dashi; multiple wheat/animal traps in one bento.
Jibuni thickens duck in wheat-soy dashi broth — classic wheat trap, not vegan.

sections.tip: Treat Kanazawa ekiben as a no-go for strict celiac; if you must eat one, plain rice-and-grilled-fish layers are the least risky but still assume wheat soy sauce — ask the vendor.

sections.verdict: Kanazawa is a wagashi capital, which is good news: many sweets are rice/bean/agar-based and naturally GF + vegan. The traps are the wheat ones (kintsuba coating, manju, monaka, castella, and Kaga fu) and any bonito-laced fermented fish like kabura-zushi. Check each box; cross-contamination is possible in shared kitchens.
sections.where: Hyakubangai あんと omiyage zone — Moroeya, Nakataya, Morihachi, Fumuroya, plus gold-leaf shops.

rows.note: Pressed mochi-rice flour and wasanbon sugar — naturally GF and vegan; a reliable Kanazawa gift.
Just mochi rice and azuki bean paste — GF and vegan; short shelf life, so eat soon.
Bean filling is plant-based but the signature thin coating is wheat flour — not GF for celiac.
Edible gold leaf is inert; check the base — agar/bean/rice versions can be GF+vegan, but castella or wheat bases are not, and gold-dusted senbei may use soy — ask.

rows.t: Kaga-bocha (roasted stem tea) 加賀棒茶
rows.note: Plain roasted tea leaves — GF and vegan; an easy, safe gift.
Fermented with yellowtail and rice-koji, often in wheat-soy seasoning — fish-based and not GF or vegan.

sections.tip: Lean on rakugan, ankoro mochi and kaga-bocha for trustworthy gifts; for kintsuba, monaka, manju, castella and Kaga fu assume wheat, and skip kabura-zushi entirely if vegan.

playbook.tight: On a <15-min connection, head straight to the Seven-Eleven Kiosk on the Shinkansen platform mezzanine (inside the gates) and build a plate from plain onigiri, cut fruit and edamame — don't gamble on a hot or seasoned item you can't read in time.
playbook.gf: Nothing in-station is celiac-certified; carry your own GF tamari, default to plain rice/fruit/nuts and naturally-GF wagashi (rakugan, ankoro mochi), and treat soy sauce, dashi, kintsuba coating and Kaga fu as wheat. When unsure, ask.
playbook.vegan: Watch hidden bonito dashi in oden, ekiben and sushi-rice seasonings; safest picks are plain konbini staples and rice/bean/agar wagashi, and for a real meal reserve Ume no Hana ahead and state vegan clearly.

nagano.name: Nagano Station 長野駅
nagano.intro: Nagano is a soba town, and soba here is the trap rather than the saviour — almost all of it is wheat-cut and the tsuyu hangs on bonito dashi. For a tight Shinkansen transfer, lean on fruit packs, apples and naturally-GF/vegan omiyage; a verified in-station sit-down meal that is both GF and vegan is hard to pin down, so plan ahead.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Best bet for a tight connection: whole fruit and packaged snacks. Hot food at the konbini is wheat-and-dashi territory.
sections.where: NewDays / NewDays MINI / KIOSK inside the Shinkansen gates; Shinano-no-Kaze and Shina-no-ki kiosks at the Shinkansen gate (approx 6:30–19:30); MIDORI depachika one floor down for fruit and veg packs.

rows.note: Nagano's signature — whole or pre-cut fruit is the cleanest GF+vegan option in the building.
Rice itself is fine, but most fillings carry wheat soy sauce or bonito; a plain shio onigiri is the closest — read the label or ask.
Plain fruit/veg is fine; skip any with dressing, custard or a mayo-based dip.
Walnuts and Nagano are a pair, but flavoured/coated snacks often add wheat, malt or dairy — check the ingredient line.
Unsweetened tea and 100% apple juice are easy wins for a quick hydration grab.

sections.tip: If the clock is against you, a bag of apples plus bottled tea is the fail-safe — don't gamble on a hot konbini item you can't verify.

sections.verdict: Confirmed — nothing verified as BOTH gluten-free AND vegan sit-down inside MIDORI Nagano; GF-capable and vegan options exist on separate axes, and the best vegan spot is a short walk from the Zenkō-ji exit, not in the building.
sections.where: MIDORI 長野 station building, 3F 'Ogosso Dining' restaurant floor (soba); Yamano-Ma Brewery is ~2 min from the Zenkō-ji exit; Zenkō-ji shukubō (temple lodgings) ~30 min walk / short bus.

rows.t: Shinshu Jūwari Soba Ten 信州十割そば てん (station front)
rows.note: 十割 = 100% buckwheat with GF tempura (buckwheat+rice flour, rice oil) and no wheat dusting — the closest station GF find — but tsuyu = bonito dashi + wheat soy, so not vegan and ask for GF tamari; at station front, likely not inside MIDORI proper.
Own site states 七割 (70% buckwheat = 30% wheat) so not GF; tempura = wheat, tsuyu = dashi + wheat soy (Kusabue official + MIDORI floor guide).

rows.t: そば処 みよ田 Miyota (MIDORI 3F)
rows.note: Mill-owned; ratio unpublished (has wheat) and dashi = kombu + bonito → not vegan, wheat soy in tsuyu → not GF (Nikkoku official + nagano-cvb).

rows.t: Yamano-Ma Brewery 山の間 (Zenkō-ji exit) — NOT in-station
rows.note: Clear star-marked vegan menu (tofu burger, spring rolls, veg hot pot), but craft beer is NOT GF, it is ~15:00–21:00 closed Tue–Wed, and a ~2-min walk — not in-station (HappyCow + Vegewel).

sections.tip: Only Nagano soba made juwari (十割, no wheat) with a wheat-free tsuyu and no shared boiling water would be GF — that combination is not verified in-station, so treat station soba as off-limits for celiac and ask in person if tempted.

sections.verdict: Nagano's ekiben are meat-and-fish heavy (beef, salmon, pork) and seasoned with wheat soy sauce; most are neither GF nor vegan. Treat as a last resort and read labels.
sections.where: Shinano-no-Kaze and Shina-no-ki at the Shinkansen gate; Meiji-tei near the MIDORI entrance; in-gate ekiben stands.

rows.note: Wheat soy sauce in the sukiyaki sauce and beef throughout — out for both diets.
Pork, miso sauce and roasted soba grains over rice — wheat in the seasoning and not plant-based.
Oyaki is a WHEAT-flour dumpling — never GF; veg-filled ones may be vegan but check for dashi/egg in the fillings.
Mixed-box bento with fish, egg and soy-seasoned sides — wheat soy and bonito throughout.

sections.tip: Ekiben labels list allergens (小麦=wheat) by law — scan that line before buying, and assume any sauce-glazed item has wheat soy sauce.

sections.verdict: Best gifts for restricted diets are apple products and agar-set Misuzu-ame; soba goods and oyaki are wheat traps despite the 'soba' name.
sections.where: MIDORI 'Shinshu Omiyage Sandō ORAHO' (1F/gate area) and station gift kiosks.

rows.note: The flagship is fruit juice + sugar + agar (kanten) — vegan and GF; but some specialty jellies add gelatin, so check '寒天 only, no ゼラチン' on that product.

rows.t: Apple products — dried apple, 100% juice, jam
rows.note: Plain dried apple/juice/jam is GF+vegan; baked apple sweets (ringo cakes) contain wheat and often dairy — those are 'no'.
Shinshu miso is rice-koji miso (rice + soybean + salt), usually wheat-free and plant-based — but confirm 'komugi' isn't listed and that it's not a dashi-blended miso.
Only genuine juwari with NO wheat is GF, and it must be cooked in clean water — most 'Shinshu soba' gifts are wheat-cut (nihachi); read for 小麦 and treat as 'ask'.
Kurumi confections are a Nagano signature but built on wheat cookie/monaka and often butter — generally not GF and frequently not vegan.
Wheat-dough dumpling — never GF; some veg fillings may be vegan but check for dashi and lard.

sections.tip: For a giftable that clears both diets, pair agar-set Misuzu-ame with plain apple juice or dried apple — and always scan the 小麦/ゼラチン allergen line.

playbook.tight: Skip the soba and the konbini hot case — grab Nagano apples or a cut-fruit pack plus bottled tea from the in-gate kiosks/depachika and run for your train.
playbook.gf: Assume all station soba is wheat-cut and every tsuyu/sauce has wheat soy sauce; safest GF buys are whole apples, plain apple products and agar Misuzu-ame. For any soba or bento, read the 小麦 allergen line and, if uncertain, ask — never assume.
playbook.vegan: Watch for hidden bonito dashi in every soba tsuyu and bento; the only verified in-area vegan sit-down is Yamano-Ma Brewery (Zenkō-ji exit, dinner-only) or, with a reservation, Zenkō-ji temple shōjin-ryōri — otherwise build a plant plate from fruit, plain veg and rice.

shin_osaka.name: Shin-Osaka Station 新大阪駅
shin_osaka.intro: Shin-Osaka is a giant Shinkansen-to-local interchange where transfers can be brutally tight, and almost every Osaka specialty here (takoyaki, okonomiyaki, 551 butaman) is wheat. For celiacs, treat this station as a grab-fruit-and-konbini-onigiri stop and save real meals for verified spots; a genuine GF/vegan sit-down restaurant inside the JR station could not be verified.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Konbini and kiosks are your fastest bet; pick whole, single-ingredient items and read labels, since most prepared foods hide wheat soy sauce and bonito dashi.
sections.where: Seven-Eleven Heart-in (inside the JR local east gate, from 06:30), Bellmart kiosks inside the Shinkansen gates, and Eki Marché エキマルシェ新大阪 takeout stands just outside the local gates.

rows.t: Salted rice onigiri (塩むすび / shio-musubi)
rows.note: Plainest onigiri is rice + salt; avoid tuna-mayo and any with soy-sauce seasoning, and check the label for wheat — ask.
Usually just rice, plum and salt, but seasoned-rice versions can carry dashi or soy — confirm the label, so ask.
Konbini bananas or a fruit cup are the cleanest no-label-needed option for a tight connection.

rows.t: Plain roasted nuts / rice-based snack packs (konbini)
rows.note: Many senbei use wheat-containing soy sauce and shared lines; only buy if the label is wheat-free, otherwise ask.
Iconic here but a wheat-flour bun with pork and soy sauce; not GF and not vegan — skip it.

sections.tip: For celiacs the safest grab is rice + salt + fruit; nothing hot off a counter here is verified gluten-free, so default to sealed, labeled items.

sections.verdict: Confirmed — no verified GF or reliable-vegan sit-down inside the JR Shin-Osaka gates (Eki Marché, Eki Marché West, concourse, Alde); the dedicated vegan+GF spot is one stop away at Osaka Station.
sections.where: Best verified GF+vegan kitchen is at Osaka/Umeda (one stop away); the vegetarian Chinese option near Shin-Osaka is in a hotel by the subway, not in the JR concourse.

rows.t: Inside JR gates (Eki Marché / Alde / concourse)
rows.note: Full Alde floor map (ramen, Botejyu, 551 Horai, sushi, tonkatsu) shows no dedicated GF/vegan venue; ramen = wheat + bonito/pork, sushi uses wheat soy — treat everything in-gate as no / ask.

rows.t: Vegan & Gluten-Free Osaka (Second Room Cafe) — Umeda, 1 stop
rows.note: 100% vegan + GF Osaka soul food (okonomiyaki, takoyaki, kushikatsu) — NOT in Shin-Osaka; it is Umeda, ~3-min walk from JR Osaka Station one stop south (own site + insideosaka).

rows.t: BelleVue Keisyoro (Chinese, veg) — hotel, outside gates
rows.note: In the Shin-Osaka Station Hotel (~2-min walk from Exit 7, outside the gates); wheat soy + shared kitchen so not GF, and the ‘vegetarian menu’ is a Vegewel-only reservation course — confirm.

sections.tip: If you truly need a verified GF+vegan meal, ride one stop to Osaka/Umeda for Vegan & Gluten-Free Osaka rather than gambling inside Shin-Osaka.

sections.verdict: Shin-Osaka has a strong ekiben lineup (Tabiben 駅弁にぎわい), but the standard bento are built on wheat soy sauce and bonito dashi, so they fail celiac and often vegan tests.
sections.where: Tabiben 駅弁にぎわい and bento counters in Eki Marché and on the Shinkansen concourse.

rows.note: Iconic soy-simmered octopus + conger in a takotsubo pot; standard recipe uses wheat soy sauce and wheat takoten, plus octopus — not GF, not vegan.

A real GF version exists (rice-noodle base, whole-soybean wheat-free soy sauce) but it is a frozen/Expo product, not the regular platform ekiben — don't assume it's on the kiosk shelf; ask, and note it still has octopus/egg so not vegan.
Marinades and tare are wheat soy-sauce based and the dish is beef — not GF, not vegan.
Looks plant-friendly but simmered veg use dashi and soy sauce; hidden bonito and wheat are likely — not GF, ask for vegan.

sections.tip: For a celiac, the only ekiben worth pursuing is Awajiya's explicit GF line — and only if a wheat-free label is physically on the box that day; otherwise ekiben here are off-limits.

sections.verdict: Osaka's headline gifts are nearly all wheat (butaman, takoyaki/okonomiyaki snacks, cheese tarts), so hunt deliberately for rice-based or dried items and still check labels.
sections.where: Eki Marché omiyage hall, the 2F/3F gift floors, and Omiyage Kaido / Daily Service souvenir counters.

rows.t: 551 Horai butaman / chimaki — AVOID for GF & vegan
rows.note: Wheat-flour bun, pork and wheat-containing soy sauce; the chimaki also has soy/wheat — neither GF nor vegan.

rows.t: Pablo / cheese tart & Osaka baked sweets
rows.note: Wheat crust plus dairy and egg — not GF, not vegan.
Wheat batter, bonito and often dairy/egg — a classic wheat trap; avoid.
Many list wheat flour and use wheat soy sauce — assume rice crackers here are NOT GF unless the label proves otherwise.
Mochi/azuki sweets can be wheat-free and egg/dairy-free, but some use wheat-starch (wasanbon mixes) or honey — read the label, so ask.
Whole umeboshi or plain nori are clean plant-based gifts; just confirm seasoned versions are free of wheat soy sauce/dashi — ask.

sections.tip: Reframe omiyage as 'rice + dried + sweet-bean' here; the flour-food Osaka is famous for is exactly what a celiac must skip.

playbook.tight: On a tight Shinkansen connection, go straight to Seven-Eleven Heart-in or a Bellmart kiosk and grab a salted/umeboshi onigiri plus fruit — read the onigiri label for wheat, and don't risk anything hot off a counter.
playbook.gf: No in-station GF restaurant is verified; for celiacs the realistic plan is sealed, labeled rice items (plain onigiri, fruit, wheat-free wagashi) at Shin-Osaka, and saving a proper GF meal for Vegan & Gluten-Free Osaka one stop away in Umeda — never assume soy sauce, dashi or ekiben are wheat-free; when unsure, ask.
playbook.vegan: Vegans can do well on plain onigiri, fruit, umeboshi, nori and bean wagashi, but watch for hidden bonito dashi in any cooked/bento item and skip butaman, octopus ekiben and sushi; for a hot vegan meal, ride one stop to Vegan & Gluten-Free Osaka in Umeda.

himeji.name: Himeji Station 姫路駅
himeji.intro: Himeji's whole castle↔station corridor is now a full curated map in this app (switch to the Himeji city) — so for a real meal, use the map. This card is the grab-&-go / ekiben / omiyage layer for a tight connection.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Konbini + the Piole depachika are your fast, label-readable options; the famous station eki-soba is wheat, so skip it for GF.
sections.where: Seven-Eleven/kiosks on the concourse; Piole Himeji depachika (fruit, veg packs, wagashi); omiyage stands.

rows.t: Plain salt onigiri, boiled egg, edamame, fruit
rows.note: The universal move — read labels; plain shio onigiri is safest.
Undressed vegetable/fruit packs; check dressing/dashi.

rows.t: Maneki 'eki-soba' 駅そば — AVOID for GF
rows.note: Himeji's iconic yellow Chinese wheat noodles in bonito dashi — wheat + fish; a landmark, but not GF or vegan.

sections.tip: Tight connection: konbini salt onigiri + edamame + a rice-flour omiyage (below), eat on board.

sections.verdict: Use the Himeji CITY MAP in this app — the castle↔station corridor has a full curated set (incl. dedicated vegan and GF-friendly spots). One in-station-area organic café is listed but single-sourced.
sections.where: Ōtemae-dōri (station↔castle) — see the Himeji city map. Piole Himeji restaurant floors.

rows.note: 120 curated corridor spots with honest GF/vegan classification — 4 vegan, 1 GF-dedicated, 1 vegan+GF among them. The real answer for a sit-down meal.
Listed on Vegewel with vegan + GF menus — single-sourced, so confirm hours & GF handling directly before going.

sections.tip: For a genuine GF/vegan meal, browse the Himeji city map rather than the station stalls.

sections.verdict: Maneki has sold Himeji ekiben for 130+ years, but they're soy-glazed eel/beef — not GF, not vegan.
sections.where: Maneki Foods stands on the concourse and platforms.

rows.note: Conger eel simmered in soy tare over dashi rice — wheat soy + eel.
Dashi rice with beef, shrimp, octopus, egg — soy and animal throughout.

sections.tip: Ekiben here are off-limits for strict GF/vegan; default to konbini + omiyage.

sections.verdict: Packaged = allergen-labeled. Nerikiri/bean wagashi and a genuine rice-flour item are the wins; the famous wheat sweets are traps.
sections.where: Piole Himeji, festa, and station omiyage counters (Iseya, Gozasōrō, etc.).

rows.t: 官兵衛 兵糧餅 (Kanbei hyōrō-mochi)
rows.note: Made with rice flour, no wheat (maker states komeko/GF) — a rare rice-based Himeji find; confirm the label & shared-facility caveat.
Nerikiri (bean + rice) wagashi — often wheat-free and plant-based, but read the label (some contain wheat/egg).
Bean filling is plant-based but the pancake batter is wheat — not GF.
Wheat sweets (and dairy/egg in the almond-toast line) — avoid.
Rice/bean/agar based — naturally GF/vegan; check for honey.

sections.tip: Hero buy: the rice-flour 兵糧餅, or plain nerikiri/yokan — read labels.

playbook.tight: Under ~15 min: konbini salt onigiri + edamame + a rice-flour omiyage (官兵衛 兵糧餅) — skip the wheat eki-soba.
playbook.gf: Real meal: open the Himeji city map (curated corridor, incl. GF-friendly spots). Quick: konbini salt onigiri, boiled egg, edamame, fruit + rice-flour 兵糧餅 / yokan. Skip eki-soba and anago ekiben (wheat).
playbook.vegan: Real meal: Himeji city map (4 vegan spots in the corridor). Quick: konbini salt onigiri + edamame + fruit + bean wagashi. Ask 'dashi wa sakana?'; skip eki-soba/ekiben.

nagoya.name: Nagoya Station 名古屋駅
nagoya.intro: Nagoya is the Tokaido Shinkansen's biggest mid-line transfer, and the honest verdict is bleak: across JR Central Towers, Takashimaya, ESCA, Unimall, Gate Walk and Gate Tower Plaza there is no dedicated gluten-free or vegan kitchen — not one of the 76 restaurants on the 12F/13F floors advertises either. Worse, Nagoya-meshi itself is a wheat minefield: miso katsu, tebasaki, kishimen, ankake spaghetti, miso nikomi udon and tenmusu are ALL wheat, and they are exactly what the complex sells. The one real gluten-free meal, Michinori-tei, is OUTSIDE the west exit — a 3-minute walk, not inside the gates.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Build a meal from single ingredients at the JR kiosks — nothing hot, prepared or Nagoya-branded near the gates is gluten-free or vegan, and the restaurant floors are a lift ride you do not have time for.
sections.where: PLUSTA Bento 北待合 and Delica Station 南待合 inside the Shinkansen gates; Bellmart and PLUSTA kiosks on the central concourse and the in-line platforms; JR Nagoya Takashimaya B1 depachika a few minutes outside the JR gates.

rows.t: Shio-musubi 塩むすび (plain salt onigiri)
rows.note: The one rice ball documented broth-free across the konbini chains — but these are JR's own PLUSTA/Bellmart brands, so read 原材料名 for 小麦 and for vinegar. Any filled or soy-seasoned onigiri is out.
The no-label-needed option; a banana or a fruit cup is the cleanest thing in the building for either diet.
Plain and unseasoned is fine; anything coated or 'flavoured' usually carries wheat soy seasoning — check the packet.

rows.t: Unsweetened soymilk 無調整豆乳 / bottled tea
rows.note: 無調整 is soybeans and water; the 調整 versions add flavourings. Unsweetened tea and 100% juice are easy wins.

rows.t: Salt hard-boiled egg 塩ゆで卵
rows.note: The white salt-brined egg is a GF protein; the brown 味付け / 煮たまご ones are marinated in soy sauce. Never vegan either way.

rows.t: Piyorin ぴよりん (the station's hero sweet) — AVOID
rows.note: Nagoya Cochin egg pudding wrapped in vanilla bavarois and rolled in powdered SPONGE — wheat sponge plus egg and dairy. The queue on the central concourse is not for you.

sections.tip: Under ~15 minutes: shio-musubi + fruit + unsweetened soymilk from PLUSTA inside the Shinkansen gates, and eat on board. Do not climb to the 12F/13F restaurant floors — the shuttle lift alone can swallow ten minutes and there is nothing up there for you.

sections.verdict: Verified: none of the 76 tenants across Towers Plaza and Gate Tower Plaza (12F–13F) advertises gluten-free or vegan. The only genuine GF meal is Michinori-tei, outside the west exit; the only in-complex accommodation is a hotel special-order you must book ahead.
sections.where: Towers Plaza 12–13F (JR Central Towers) and Gate Tower Plaza 12–13F (JR Gate Tower), both via the shuttle lifts from 2F; Nagoya Marriott Associa Hotel 15F/18F sits in the same towers. Michinori-tei is ~3 min on foot from the west (Taiko-dori) exit.

rows.t: Michinori-tei みちのり亭 — OUTSIDE the west exit
rows.note: Fully gluten-free washoku: 「小麦はもちろん、大麦、ライ麦、オーツ麦など、グルテンを含む穀物を一切使用しない」, 米粉 rice-flour breading, wheat-free tamari, separated equipment, owner has a wheat allergy; FindMeGlutenFree lists it as dedicated. Two caveats: the shop itself warns some condiment factories also handle wheat, and nhkomorebi.com — quoted everywhere as corroboration — is the owner's OWN blog, so it is not independent. Meat- and fish-centred, so vegans must ask.

The hotel directly above the tracks publishes vegan courses (Pergola Western ¥7,000–9,000, Tsuruya kaiseki ¥12,000; 2 guests minimum, 1 week ahead) and a gluten-free à la carte at Pergola (from ¥5,000 lunch, 1 guest, same-day possible). This is the hotel's own single claim with no dedicated-kitchen protocol published — a celiac must confirm handling on 052-584-1157 before relying on it.

rows.t: やさい家めい (Gate Tower Plaza 13F)
rows.note: Vegetable-forward izakaya and the one 12F/13F tenant Vegewel tags vegan-compatible, but nothing vegan or GF is published on its own menu and the kitchen runs on dashi and wheat soy sauce — confirm dish by dish.

rows.t: 元気になる農場レストラン モクモク (Towers Plaza 13F)
rows.note: Farm restaurant with real vegetables, but the bread and noodle lines are wheat and the simmered sides and dressings use dashi and soy — no GF or vegan menu is published.

rows.t: Vegewel's 'Nagoya Station' list — STALE, verify first
rows.note: ソラノイロ名古屋 closed in 2020; ダーシェンカ is not in Takashimaya's current bakery line-up (rebuilt Jun 2026 as BOUL'ANGE / Maison Kayser / Pompadour); 涵梅舫 is in the Meitetsu Grand Hotel 18F, not the JR complex. Do not plan a meal off that list without phoning ahead.
つけめんTETSU, 讃岐うどん 野らぼー, とんかつ 恵亭, 鉄板・お好み焼き 電光石火, 天ぷら新宿つな八 — wheat noodles, panko, batter and wheat-soy tare, on shared fryers and shared boiling water.

sections.tip: With 45 minutes and a celiac in the party, walk out the west (Taiko-dori) exit to Michinori-tei rather than riding up to 12F/13F — you will find nothing gluten-free up there. And do not go looking for 近鉄パッセ or the 名鉄百貨店 food floors: both closed permanently on 28 Feb 2026 in the Meieki redevelopment.

sections.h: Nagoya-meshi — say it plainly: it is a wheat minefield
sections.verdict: Nearly every dish Nagoya is famous for is wheat, and not in a way you can ask around. The wheat is in the batter, the noodle and the flour dusting — not just the glaze — so 'sauce on the side' fixes nothing.
sections.where: ESCA underground mall at the Shinkansen (west) exit — 矢場とん miso katsu, 山本屋本店 miso nikomi udon, 千寿 tenmusu; 住よし kishimen stands on the Shinkansen and in-line platforms; スパゲティハウス チャオ (ankake spaghetti) in Gate Tower Plaza 12F.

rows.t: Miso katsu みそかつ (矢場とん, ESCA)
rows.note: Pork cutlet in PANKO breadcrumbs — wheat before the sauce even arrives, on a fryer shared with everything else. Pork, so never vegan.
Dusted in 小麦粉 (wheat flour) before frying, then painted with a sweet wheat-soy tare — wheat twice over, and chicken. Furaibo and Yamachan style are the same recipe.

rows.t: Kishimen きしめん (住よし, platform stands)
rows.note: Flat WHEAT noodles in a bonito-dashi and soy broth at the stand-up counters on the platforms. A beloved 60-year institution and a celiac/vegan double no.

rows.t: Miso nikomi udon 味噌煮込みうどん (山本屋本店, ESCA)
rows.note: Udon is wheat by definition, and the hatcho-miso broth is built on bonito dashi with an egg dropped in.

rows.t: Ankake spaghetti あんかけスパ (チャオ, Gate Tower Plaza 12F)
rows.note: Wheat pasta under a peppery sauce thickened with a wheat-flour roux, usually over sausage or ham. No component of it is gluten-free.
It looks like the safe rice ball in the case and it is not: the filling is shrimp TEMPURA — wheat batter, plus shrimp. This one catches people.
Eel glazed in a wheat-soy tare over dashi rice, and the tea broth you pour over the last third is dashi as well.

rows.t: Hatcho miso 八丁味噌 itself (the exception)
rows.speed: 🎁 as a gift, not a meal
rows.note: The paste alone is genuinely soy and salt — see Omiyage below. But every restaurant dish built on it adds dashi, soy sauce or a wheat coating, so the miso being clean does not make miso katsu or miso nikomi safe.

sections.tip: There is no gluten-free version of Nagoya-meshi anywhere in the station complex. The only kitchen in the city that rebuilds these exact dishes without gluten grain is Michinori-tei, three minutes out the west exit.

sections.verdict: Nagoya's ekiben are Nagoya-meshi in a box — miso katsu, tebasaki, eel, Nagoya Cochin chicken, even a Taiwan-ramen collab — so they inherit every wheat and dashi trap. Nothing here is certified gluten-free and nothing is vegan.
sections.where: Delica Station 名古屋コンコース and PLUSTA Bento 北待合 inside the Shinkansen gates; PLUSTA 名古屋中央 on the central concourse; 松浦商店 kiosk on in-line platforms 10/11.

rows.note: Panko cutlet and flour-dusted wings under a wheat-soy tare — the two worst Nagoya dishes for a celiac, boxed together.
Eel in a wheat-soy-mirin glaze over dashi-seasoned rice.

rows.t: Nagoya Cochin 名古屋コーチン chicken bento
rows.note: Prized local chicken simmered in soy and mirin over dashi rice, usually with a soy-marinated egg alongside.

rows.t: 矢場味仙 Taiwan-ramen bento (松浦商店, from Feb 2026)
rows.note: The newest box on the shelf and one of the worst for both diets: wheat noodles plus spicy pork mince.
The only conceivable fallback, but pickles, furikake and simmered sides routinely carry soy sauce and bonito — inspect every compartment, and note bonito dashi can legally go unlabelled.

sections.tip: Boxes carry the legal allergen line, so scan for 小麦 before you pay — but assume every glaze is wheat soy sauce and every seasoned rice is dashi-cooked. A shio-musubi and fruit from PLUSTA is the safer buy.

sections.verdict: Two real wins here, and one of them sits inches from a trap: Kakukyu's hatcho miso is 大豆と塩のみ, while the miso-katsu tare bottles on the same shelf carry wheat and mackerel. Aoyagi uiro is rice-flour by recipe but wheat by its own allergen label.
sections.where: JR Nagoya Takashimaya B1 depachika (東海の味 miso counter); PLUSTA Gift and Gift Kiosk counters on the concourse and by the Shinkansen gates; ESCA omiyage row (青柳ういろう); Gate Walk B1 and Unimall gift stands.

rows.t: Kakukyu hatcho miso 八丁味噌 (Takashimaya B1)
rows.note: The maker's own label reads 「大豆（三河産）、食塩」 with 大豆 as the only declared allergen — soybeans and salt, aged two summers under stones in cedar vats. No wheat, no dashi, no animal: the best GF+vegan gift in the building.

rows.t: Miso-katsu tare みそかつのたれ (same shelf) — AVOID
rows.note: Sold beside the miso and NOT the same thing: the label carries 風味調味料（小麦、さばを含む） — wheat AND mackerel. Buy the plain miso; never the tare.

rows.t: Aoyagi uiro 青柳ういろう (ESCA, KITTE Nagoya)
rows.note: The maker states the base is うるち米の米粉 (non-glutinous rice flour) — no wheat in the recipe, no egg or dairy on the label. BUT Aoyagi's own 特定原材料等28品目 line on every uiro box declares 小麦, because the same factory turns out きしめんパイ and カエルまんじゅう. Fine for a gluten-avoider; a celiac should treat it as a shared-wheat plant.

rows.t: Yasunaga-mochi 安永餅 (永餅屋老舗)
rows.note: The maker's own ingredient line is 餅米・砂糖・小豆・水飴・上新粉 — all rice and bean, no wheat, no additives, no animal. It is reported on sale at the station kiosks and in ESCA, but that stocking is blog-sourced and the shared-facility question is unanswered, so read the box in your hand.

rows.t: Nishio matcha 西尾の抹茶 / plain leaf tea
rows.note: Aichi is Japan's matcha heartland and plain ground tea is just leaf — an easy, safe, distinctly local gift. Skip the latte mixes and matcha sweets, which add milk powder and wheat.
The most-bought Nagoya gift and useless to a celiac: dried WHEAT noodles with a soup sachet that is usually bonito dashi and wheat soy sauce.

rows.t: Ebi senbei ゆかり (坂角総本舖)
rows.note: Nagoya's signature prawn cracker declares えび・小麦 — shrimp and wheat flour. Off on both counts.

rows.t: Piyorin / カエルまんじゅう / 名古屋 生サブレ
rows.note: Wheat sponge, manju and sable with egg and dairy — the famous cute ones are all out.

sections.tip: Hero buy: a tub of Kakukyu hatcho miso from the Takashimaya B1 東海の味 counter — genuinely gluten-free, genuinely vegan, and unmistakably Nagoya. Just leave the tare bottle on the shelf.

playbook.tight: Under ~15 min: shio-musubi + fruit + unsweetened soymilk from PLUSTA or Delica Station inside the Shinkansen gates, and eat on board. Skip every Nagoya-meshi counter — miso katsu, tebasaki, kishimen and tenmusu are all wheat — and do not ride up to the 12F/13F restaurant floors.
playbook.gf: Treat the whole complex as wheat: miso katsu is panko, tebasaki is flour-dusted, kishimen and miso nikomi udon are wheat noodles, ankake spaghetti is wheat pasta in a flour roux, and tenmusu is tempura. Nothing on the 76-tenant restaurant floors is gluten-free. For a real meal, walk 3 minutes out the WEST (Taiko-dori) exit to Michinori-tei — fully gluten-grain-free, rice-flour breading, wheat-free tamari — remembering that nhkomorebi.com is the owner's own blog and not independent corroboration, and that the shop itself flags some condiment suppliers as wheat-handling. Otherwise: shio-musubi, fruit, nuts, and Kakukyu hatcho miso as the gift. Aoyagi uiro is rice flour by recipe but declares 小麦 on its own label — gluten-avoider yes, celiac no.
playbook.vegan: Bonito dashi is in every broth, every seasoned rice and most 'vegetable' sides, and the miso dishes are no exception. Safe picks are shio-musubi, fruit, edamame, unsweetened soymilk, Kakukyu hatcho miso (大豆と塩のみ), Aoyagi uiro, 安永餅 and Nishio matcha. For a hot vegan meal in the complex the only published option is the Marriott Associa's course (Pergola 15F or Kyoto Tsuruya 18F) — 2 guests, booked a week ahead. Vegewel's Nagoya Station list is stale: ソラノイロ closed in 2020 and 涵梅舫 is in the Meitetsu Grand Hotel, not the JR complex.

nara.name: Nara Stations 奈良駅
nara.intro: Nara has two 'Nara Stations' about 1 km apart and travellers book the wrong one constantly: JR Nara 奈良駅 (JR West, with the Vierra Nara station building) sits west of the centre, while Kintetsu Nara 近鉄奈良駅 (underground, Kintetsu Nara Line from Osaka-Namba/Kyoto) puts you a five-minute walk from Nara Park, Higashimuki arcade and Naramachi — the 12–15 min walk between them along Sanjo-dori is the difference between 'I'm there' and 'I'm still walking'. Neither station has a verified gluten-free or vegan sit-down restaurant inside it, so the honest floor here is a konbini shio-musubi, and every genuine GF/vegan kitchen in Nara is on foot from the KINTETSU side. Nara's own specialities are traps you have to know by name: kakinoha-zushi carries wheat on the makers' own labels, Miwa somen is flat-out wheat, and the only explicitly gluten-free kuzu shop is at a third station entirely.

sections.h: Two 'Nara Stations' — know which one you're at
sections.verdict: Kintetsu Nara is the one you almost certainly want: it has a konbini INSIDE the gates and puts Naramachi, the park and every GF/vegan kitchen within walking distance. JR Nara has no in-gate konbini — but it has a full supermarket.
sections.where: JR Nara 奈良駅 (Yamatoji/Nara lines; Vierra Nara station building) and Kintetsu Nara 近鉄奈良駅 (underground; Time's Place Nara concourse) are ~1 km / 12–15 min apart on foot along Sanjo-dori; frequent buses run between them.

rows.note: The useful one. FamilyMart 近鉄奈良駅改札内店 is INSIDE the ticket gates (approx 5:45–23:15) — the only in-gate konbini at either station. The exit opens onto Higashimuki arcade → Mochiidono → Naramachi. No verified GF or vegan restaurant in the station itself.

rows.t: JR Nara 奈良駅 (Vierra Nara station building)
rows.note: No konbini inside the gates — Seven-Eleven Heart-in JR奈良駅改札口 is OUTSIDE (approx 6:30–22:00). Compensates with KOHYO supermarket on Vierra 1F (approx 7:00–24:00), the best-stocked label-reading option in either building. Nara Park and Naramachi need a bus or a long walk.

A flat, straight shopping street — fine with a suitcase, but budget it: arriving at JR when your hotel or your reserved vegan lunch is by Kintetsu costs you a quarter of an hour you probably didn't plan.

sections.tip: If you get to choose, book to Kintetsu Nara — and if a train only serves JR Nara, do your food shopping at KOHYO on Vierra 1F before you start walking.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: Doable at Kintetsu (konbini inside the gates); at JR you must step outside the gates, so allow an extra few minutes. Assemble a meal from single-ingredient items rather than trusting anything prepared.
sections.where: Kintetsu: FamilyMart inside the gates (approx 5:45–23:15); Time's Place Nara concourse shops just outside. JR: Seven-Eleven Heart-in outside the gates (approx 6:30–22:00), KOHYO supermarket Vierra 1F (approx 7:00–24:00), Nara no Umaimono Plaza Vierra 1F (approx 7:00–21:00).

rows.t: Shio-musubi 塩むすび (plain salt rice ball)
rows.note: The floor of this station, and the one onigiri documented broth-free at all three konbini chains — most-likely-OK, not guaranteed. Scan the label for 小麦; some salted rice is vinegared. Avoid filled onigiri: soy-sauce seasoning and bonito are the norm.

A real supermarket attached to JR Nara — plain tofu, natto (leave the tare packet), salted edamame, undressed cut vegetables, whole fruit, unsweetened 無調整 soymilk, all with full 原材料名 lines to read. Far more choice than either konbini; nothing is certified GF.

rows.t: 箱夢 HAKOYUME onigiri stand (Kintetsu Nara, outside gates)
rows.speed: ⚡ made to order, approx weekdays 7:00–19:00 / weekends 9:30–19:00
rows.note: Kintetsu-group onigiri specialist in Time's Place, rice cooked and shaped after you order (Tsuya-hime rice). No published allergen list and no GF/vegan programme, so ask for a salt-only one and confirm the seasoning — a nicer rice ball than the konbini, not a safer one.
The no-label-needed pick at both stations; pure fruit with no syrup or dressing.

rows.t: Unsweetened soymilk 無調整豆乳 / bottled tea
rows.note: 無調整 is soybeans and water; 調整 versions add flavourings. Unsweetened tea and 100% juice are safe hydration for both diets.

rows.t: Salt hard-boiled egg 塩ゆでたまご
rows.note: The salt-brined (塩) one needs no sauce and is normally wheat-free — but skip the brown 味付け/煮たまご, which are soy-sauce marinated. Never vegan.

rows.t: Coffee: Cafe Ciao Presso (Kintetsu) / Starbucks JR Nara old station building
rows.note: Ciao Presso & YAMATO BREWERY sits on the Kintetsu concourse from about 7:00; Starbucks is in the old JR station building ~2 min from the JR gates. Black coffee and tea are fine for both diets; Starbucks stocks soy/oat milk but has NO gluten-free food, and both food cases are wheat pastry and sandwiches.

sections.tip: At Kintetsu, in-gate FamilyMart + shio-musubi + fruit and you're on the train. At JR, don't hunt inside the gates — there is nothing there; go out to KOHYO.

sections.verdict: No verified GF or vegan sit-down exists inside either station — Time's Place Nara and Vierra Nara are conventional udon/soba, yoshoku, izakaya and kaiseki. Nara's genuine GF and vegan kitchens are all a short walk from KINTETSU Nara, none from JR.
sections.where: Inside: Time's Place Nara concourse (Kintetsu) and Vierra Nara 1F (JR). Outside: Higashimuki and Naramachi, 3–10 min on foot from Kintetsu Nara.

rows.t: ならまちヴィーガン 菜美 nabi — NOT in-station
rows.note: The real answer for a celiac in Nara: a fully dedicated kitchen that keeps wheat, buckwheat and peanuts out entirely, umami from kombu/shiitake, everything on the menu vegan (own site + Vegewel + local press). In Naramachi (Higashishiodo-cho) — check the clock and the calendar: approx 12:00–17:00 and CLOSED Tue/Wed/Thu, and severe restrictions are asked to contact ahead.

100% vegan macrobiotic cafe built on sprouted brown rice, with house-made brown-rice noodles; own site says 添加物・グルテン不使用, but that is essentially a single self-claim with no celiac-grade corroboration of actual handling — genuinely vegan, GF stays at ask. Hours vary by season; confirm.

rows.t: Vegan Ramen by Playpen Friends — NOT in-station
rows.speed: 🪑 ~5 min walk from Kintetsu, approx 11:00–17:00 cl. Tue
rows.note: Six clearly-labelled vegan ramen styles by Nara Park — but the noodles are wheat (never GF) and the same kitchen also cooks genuine tonkotsu and chicken paitan, so a strict vegan should confirm separate handling.

The Low-Allergen ポークサンド〈米粉〉 on a 100% rice-flour bun, heated sealed in its bag, is the most celiac-defensible fast-food item in either building — but MOS itself does not certify it gluten-free, it is PORK so never vegan, the fries share a fryer, and you must confirm this branch stocks the low-allergen line.

rows.t: Inside the stations: Time's Place Nara / Vierra Nara 1F
rows.note: Udon and soba (wheat noodles, bonito-and-wheat-soy tsuyu), teishoku, yoshoku, izakaya and Yamato kaiseki such as 月日亭 by the Kintetsu gates — dashi and wheat soy sauce run through all of it. No dedicated GF or vegan venue appears in either directory.

rows.t: 古都華 Kotoka, Nara no Umaimono Plaza (Vierra Nara 1F)
rows.note: Farm-direct Nara restaurant whose lunch set comes with a Nara-vegetable buffet — the most plant-forward thing physically inside either station, and it opens at 7:00. But it is a conventional kitchen (egg-on-rice breakfasts, Yamato pork and beef at dinner) with no published GF or vegan menu; simmered vegetables and dressings will normally carry dashi and wheat soy sauce. Ask, item by item.

sections.tip: For a real GF or vegan meal, get off at Kintetsu Nara, not JR — and check nabi's closed days (Tue/Wed/Thu) before you build a day around it.

sections.verdict: Nara's ekiben IS kakinoha-zushi, and the makers' own labels rule it out: Izasa/Nakatani Honpo lists 醤油 in the ingredients and declares 小麦・さけ・さば・大豆, and Tanaka's Nara honten posts えび・小麦・卵. 'Persimmon-leaf sushi is wheat-free by recipe' is folklore — it is fish, and it is labelled wheat.
sections.where: ゐざさ寿司 奈良駅売店 on the Kintetsu concourse (outside gates, approx 10:00–19:00); 柿の葉すし本舗たなか inside 奈良銘品館 at the JR central gate; Tanaka's 柿の葉茶屋 eat-in at the Higashimuki arcade entrance by Kintetsu Nara.

rows.t: 柿の葉寿司 kakinoha-zushi (ゐざさ / 中谷本舗)
rows.note: The maker's own ingredient list runs 酢飯 … 酢〆さば・さけ・あじ・真鯛 … 醤油, with the allergen line 小麦・さけ・さば・大豆. Wheat via the soy sauce, and cured fish throughout — out on both counts.

rows.t: 柿の葉すし (柿の葉すし本舗たなか)
rows.note: The Nara honten posts えび・小麦・卵, and the eat-in sets come with miso soup containing 麩 (wheat gluten). Same verdict as Izasa: no.

rows.t: 五目ちらし / 蒸し寿司 / variety boxes
rows.note: The rest of the Nara bento shelf is simmered vegetables and fish in dashi and soy-mirin seasoning, plus egg — wheat and animal ingredients in every layer.

rows.t: 箱夢 made-to-order onigiri as the ekiben substitute
rows.note: If you want something rice-based to carry onto the train, a plain salt onigiri ordered at the counter beats every bento here — but it is an 'ask', not a safe: no allergen programme, shared prep.

sections.tip: Nara's signature bento is a wheat-and-fish trap on the makers' own labels — for a celiac or vegan the real 'ekiben' here is a konbini shio-musubi plus fruit, bought before you pass the gate.

sections.verdict: Packaged means allergen-labelled, and Nara's gift shelves split cleanly: kuzu (arrowroot) and rice/bean wagashi are the wins, Miwa somen and the sushi are flat wheat. Know the catch — Tenkyudo's explicitly gluten-free kuzu shop is at Kintetsu Department Store in Yamato-Saidaiji, NOT at either Nara station.
sections.where: JR side (Vierra Nara 2F): 奈良銘品館, 天極堂 (approx 10:00–18:00), 山崎屋 narazuke, 光悦, 極うめもり, 奈良みやこ路. Kintetsu side (Time's Place Nara): GOTO-CHI奈良 (approx 9:00–20:00), 天極堂奈良駅店 (approx 10:00–19:00), 千壽庵吉宗 (approx 10:30–18:30, cl. Wed/Thu), たまうさぎ玉兎 (approx 10:00–18:00, cl. Mon/Tue), まほろば大仏プリン.

rows.t: 吉野本葛 Yoshino hon-kuzu — 天極堂 (both stations)
rows.note: Kuzu starch is naturally wheat-free and Tenkyudo itself markets it as a gluten-free flour substitute — but the two station shops are general shops with an eat-in menu, not the GF line. Their dedicated グルテンフリー葛スイーツ specialty shop (くずの子ロール, 100% kuzu, no wheat flour) is in the basement of Kintetsu Department Store Nara at YAMATO-SAIDAIJI station, not here. Kinako and kuromitsu toppings are plant-based; check for honey.

rows.t: 生わらび餅 — 千壽庵吉宗 (Kintetsu concourse, cl. Wed/Thu)
rows.note: Warabimochi is natural starch, sugar and kinako; the retail listing for the plain pack declares no 特定原材料 at all, which is real evidence — but that covers only the 8 mandatory allergens and says nothing about the facility. Genuinely close to a GF+vegan gift; still ask.

rows.t: きなこだんご たまうさぎ 玉兎 (Kintetsu concourse, cl. Mon/Tue)
rows.note: Domestic Hinohikari rice pounded to mochi, coated in a house 蜜 syrup and kinako — no wheat by recipe, and no allergen programme either. Confirm the 蜜 is sugar syrup rather than honey, and note it is same-day eating.

rows.t: 中谷堂 yomogi-mochi (Mochiidono, ~4 min from Kintetsu)
rows.speed: ⚡ approx 10:00–18:00, cl. Tue, until sold out
rows.note: The famous high-speed mochi-pounding stand: glutinous rice, mugwort, Tokachi red bean paste and kinako — wheat-free by recipe and plant-based as documented. But it is a small artisan counter with no published allergen list, no celiac handling and shared equipment, so ask rather than assume.

rows.t: 奈良漬 narazuke (山崎屋, Vierra Nara 2F)
rows.note: Melon, cucumber and gourd re-pickled over months in sake lees and mirin lees — both rice-derived, so usually no wheat and no animal ingredient, but there is no published allergen list, and kizami/miso-dressed versions add miso (which can be barley) or amino-acid seasoning. Also genuinely alcoholic — not for children or drivers.

Nara's signature noodle is wheat flour, full stop — never GF. The dried noodles themselves are plant-based, but the tsuyu bundled with gift boxes is bonito dashi plus wheat soy sauce, so a vegan should buy the noodles alone.

rows.t: まほろば大仏プリン / baked and Western sweets
rows.note: The deer-lid pudding is egg and dairy — never vegan; the custard itself is usually wheat-free but there is no GF programme and the same counters sell wheat cakes and monaka. Treat all baked omiyage here as wheat unless the label proves otherwise.

sections.tip: Hero buy: kuzu from 天極堂, or a box of 千壽庵吉宗 warabimochi — starch-and-bean based, plant-based by recipe, allergen-labelled. Just don't upgrade them to 'safe', and remember the certified-GF kuzu counter is at Yamato-Saidaiji, not here.

playbook.tight: Which gate you're at decides everything. Kintetsu Nara: the FamilyMart is INSIDE the ticket gates (approx 5:45–23:15) — shio-musubi, fruit, unsweetened soymilk, done. JR Nara: there is NO konbini inside the gates; Seven-Eleven Heart-in is outside (approx 6:30–22:00) and KOHYO supermarket on Vierra 1F (approx 7:00–24:00) is a minute further and far better stocked, so buy before you pass through.
playbook.gf: Nothing at either station is certified gluten-free, and Nara's specialities are the trap: both big kakinoha-zushi makers declare 小麦 on their own labels (soy sauce in the rice seasoning), Miwa somen is wheat, and every station soba/udon is wheat with bonito-and-wheat-soy tsuyu. Build from single-ingredient items — shio-musubi, fruit, plain nuts, salt egg, KOHYO's tofu and undressed vegetables — plus rice/kuzu wagashi, scanning every box for 小麦. The one defensible fast option is MOS Burger's Low-Allergen rice-flour pork bun on Vierra 1F (not certified, and pork). For a real GF meal, walk from KINTETSU Nara to Naramachi Vegan nabi — a dedicated wheat-free kitchen, approx 12:00–17:00, closed Tue/Wed/Thu.
playbook.vegan: Dashi is the whole battle in Nara: Yamato kaiseki, chagayu, simmered vegetables and every noodle tsuyu in these two stations run on bonito, and 'vegetable' sides are no exception. The reliable floor is shio-musubi, fruit, salted edamame, plain tofu and unsweetened soymilk; kuzu, warabimochi, kinako dango and yomogi-mochi are plant-based by recipe — just check the syrup for honey. For a hot vegan meal get off at Kintetsu Nara: KURURU (~3 min, 100% vegan macrobiotic) or Naramachi Vegan nabi (~8–10 min, fully vegan and wheat-free); Vegan Ramen by Playpen Friends has a real vegan menu but shares its kitchen with tonkotsu. Always ask 'dashi wa sakana desu ka?'

toba.name: Toba & Ise Stations 鳥羽駅・伊勢市駅
toba.intro: Be honest about the scale: these are small stations, and for a tight connection at Toba the real answer is that there is a konbini and that is it. Ise is materially better provisioned — Iseshi has a FamilyMart on the Kintetsu platform INSIDE the gates, a 24-hour konbini 180 m out the north side, and Akafuku kiosks open from 06:00 — so if you can choose where to be hungry, be hungry in Ise. Almost every famous food here is a trap: Ise udon is emphatically wheat noodles in a tamari-soy tare, tekone-zushi is soy-marinated fish, and Toba's grilled shellfish gets a soy brush, so plan to assemble a meal from rice, fruit and two or three clean wagashi rather than to eat a speciality.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: There is a konbini, and that is it. Nothing gluten-free or vegan is cooked to order at any of these three stations, and at Toba there is no shop at all inside the gates.
sections.where: Toba: FamilyMart 近鉄鳥羽駅改札外橋上店, outside the gates on the overhead concourse ~45 m from the platforms, 06:00–20:00 — the only konbini in the building. Iseshi: FamilyMart on Kintetsu platform 4, INSIDE the gates, 06:00–20:00, plus 24-hour FamilyMart 伊勢本町店 ~180 m out the north side. Ujiyamada: FamilyMart in Time's Place うじやまだ 1F, outside the gates, 06:00–21:00 (the old platform-4 store closed in 2022).

rows.t: Shio-musubi 塩むすび (plain salt rice ball)
rows.note: The one konbini rice ball documented broth-free at all three chains, and the single most useful item in this whole area — scan the label for 小麦 and note that some use vinegared rice. Filled onigiri carry wheat soy sauce or bonito.
No label to read; the cleanest grab in a station with no kitchen you can question.
Plain versions are fine; coated or flavoured nuts and snack mixes usually add wheat soy seasoning — check.
無調整 is soybeans and water; 調整 versions add flavourings. The easiest calories at 06:00 in Toba.

Mochi rice, Hokkaido azuki and sugar; the only allergen Akafuku declares is 大豆 (soy, inside its 糖類加工品 sugar blend) and no wheat — but there is no wheat-free-facility claim, so it stays 'ask' for a celiac. Eat it the same day.

rows.t: まる天 鳥羽駅店 fish-paste sticks (Toba Stn, 09:00–18:00)
rows.note: The obvious hot snack at Toba Station and a double fail — surimi fish paste, wheat in the batter and binder, deep-fried in a shared fryer.

sections.tip: At Toba, buy before you arrive or accept the FamilyMart — its one konbini shuts at 20:00 and there is nothing inside the gates. The 24-hour fallbacks are Lawson 鳥羽一丁目 and FamilyMart 鳥羽中央, both a few hundred metres out of the station.

sections.verdict: No dedicated GF and no dedicated vegan kitchen exists at any of these three stations, on the shrine approach, or in Toba — the two curated stops are a single-source rice-flour sweet shop at Iseshi Station front and a modifiable café out at Futami.
sections.where: Iseshi Station front (本町2-1 駅前ビル 1F) for Yamada Sanpou, 2 min from the gates; 外宮参道 between Iseshi Station and the Outer Shrine; Ise Meoto Yokocho at Futami (near Meoto Iwa, one stop up the JR line toward Ise) for Chaya Ukanomitama; Toba's Sazae Street, 2 min from the south exit.

rows.t: Yamada Sanpou 山田三方 (Iseshi Stn front)
rows.note: Rice-flour 三方焼. The entire GF claim traces to ONE source — the owner's own 2024 announcement that the batter and the custard/choco creams are 米粉 — and the shop's current homepage no longer mentions 米粉 or グルテンフリー at all, with no allergen statement anywhere. Only the あずき version is plant-based (custard, choco and ice cream are not). Phone 070-8978-0276 and confirm no wheat is handled on site before serving a celiac child.

rows.t: Chaya Ukanomitama 茶屋ウカノミタマ (Futami, Meoto Yokocho)
rows.note: The operator's own copy advertises 「グルテンフリーの軽食とおやつ」 with own-farm organic produce, and Vegewel lists vegan/vegetarian modification as possible — but it is a shared tourist-market kitchen with no celiac-specific or wheat-free claim. Ask exactly which items are GF and how they are prepared.

rows.t: Sazae Street plain-grilled shellfish (鈴木水産 and neighbours, Toba)
rows.note: 素焼き (plain-grilled) oysters, sazae, abalone and sashimi are naturally wheat-free, but the sazae tsuboyaki broth and every dipping sauce are wheat-brewed soy and the grill and brush are shared. Ask for it grilled plain, no soy, no shared brush — and it is never vegan.

rows.t: Ise udon anywhere (ふくすけ, station-area shops, Toba udon houses)
rows.note: THE local dish and the biggest trap here. The noodles are wheat — ふくすけ's hand-made version is 100% Mie-grown 小麦 — and the dark tare is tamari soy sauce with kombu and katsuobushi. Emphatically not gluten-free, and not vegan as served.

rows.t: Toba/Ise seafood shokudo, sushi counters and kaisen-don
rows.note: Sashimi over plain rice is the only realistic celiac path, and every soy sauce, tare and simmered side is wheat-brewed — bring your own GF tamari. Nothing on this coast is plant-based.

sections.tip: Ise is the better base and it is not close: Iseshi Station gives you a konbini inside the gates, a 24-hour konbini 180 m away and a rice-flour sweet shop 2 minutes out. Toba gives you a konbini and a shellfish grill.

sections.h: Okage-yokocho & Oharaimachi — where you'll actually eat
sections.verdict: This is where travellers really eat, and Okage-yokocho has done something rare and honest: ふくすけ publishes a dietary sheet that tells celiacs plainly it cannot feed them and sends them up the lane for a salt rice ball.
sections.where: Oharaimachi, the ~800 m approach from the Uji Bridge at Naiku, with Okage-yokocho in the middle of it. Most shops ~10:00–17:00 (L.O. 16:30); 赤福本店 is the exception at 05:00–17:00. From Iseshi/Ujiyamada it is a bus ride to 内宮前.

rows.t: ふくすけ dietary sheet 「宗教食のお客様へ」 (Okage-yokocho)
rows.note: The shop's own sheet, hosted on okageyokocho.com, states that Ise udon noodles contain wheat, that they only serve Ise udon, and that 団五郎茶屋 nearby offers a salt rice ball — an explicit written 'we cannot feed a celiac'. For vegans it says the tare contains seafood such as mackerel and bonito, that they can serve the udon without sauce, and that they can provide salt — which is still a wheat noodle.

rows.t: 団五郎茶屋 salt rice ball 塩おにぎり (Okage-yokocho)
rows.note: Named by ふくすけ's sheet as the gluten-free fallback, and Dangoro does hand-form onigiri from Tsuyahime rice to order — but Dangoro's own page lists no plain 塩おにぎり, its seasonal onigiri are things like eel, and it is primarily a soba house (wheat-cut Togakushi soba in dashi broth) with shared hands and counters. Ask for 塩むすび by name and confirm no dashi in the rice.

rows.t: 赤福餅 at 赤福本店 (05:00–17:00)
rows.note: Mochi rice, Hokkaido azuki, sugar — plant-based, and no wheat is declared (the only allergen-tier item is 大豆, from the 糖類加工品 sugar blend). But there is NO wheat-free-facility claim and Akafuku itself handles a gluten grain: the 1 June 朔日餅 is 麦手餅, made with 麦こがし and もち麦粉 (barley). Opens at 05:00 with the dawn shrine visit.

rows.t: 赤福ぜんざい (winter, ¥800, served in-shop)
rows.note: The trap is the side dish, not the bowl: Akafuku's own page states 「塩ふき昆布」に小麦、大豆が含まれます — the salted-kelp palate cleanser served alongside contains wheat. The zenzai itself is azuki, sugar, mochi and potato starch. Leave the kelp. (赤福氷, the summer shaved ice, lists no allergens at all.)

rows.t: てこね寿司 (すし久 and most approach restaurants)
rows.note: Ise-Shima's other signature: bonito or tuna marinated in a soy-based tare over vinegared rice, usually finished with shredded egg. Wheat soy sauce and fish — out on both counts.

rows.t: 豚捨 croquette, 松阪牛串, 伊勢うどん stalls, baked approach sweets
rows.note: The whole walk-and-eat lineup is wheat batter, wheat soy tare or wheat sponge, cooked on shared griddles and fryers. Assume no unless a shop hands you a written ingredient list.

sections.tip: Screenshot the ふくすけ sheet before you go (okageyokocho.com → ふくすけ → 宗教食のお客様へ). It is the only written dietary statement on the entire approach, it is honest, and showing it to staff makes the 塩おにぎり request instantly legible.

sections.h: Ekiben — station bento (there basically aren't any)
sections.verdict: Say it plainly: Iseshi and Ujiyamada sell no ekiben, and Toba's 'ekiben' is a made-to-order seafood box in the mall next door. Nothing here is GF or vegan.
sections.where: 鳥羽1番街, joined to Toba Station by a passage (09:30–17:30, to 18:00 weekends/holidays) — 鳥羽弁当 at 海鮮茶屋えびしま on 3F, cooked after you order. The nearest real ekiben counter is あら竹 beside the JR gates at Matsusaka, ~40 min up the line.

rows.t: 鳥羽弁当 (Toba Ichibangai 3F, made to order)
rows.note: A city-certified box built on Toba's fish and shellfish with soy-based seasoning; it is cooked on order so timing is unpredictable, and it fails both diets outright.

rows.t: Konbini bento at any of the three stations
rows.note: Fried items share a common batter, sauces are wheat-brewed soy, and simmered sides carry bonito dashi that the label is not required to declare. Build a meal from single-ingredient parts instead.

rows.t: モー太郎弁当 / あら竹 (JR Matsusaka, ~40 min away)
rows.note: The region's famous ekiben — A5 wagyu sukiyaki in a secret tare. Wheat soy sauce plus beef; worth knowing about only so you do not detour for it.

sections.tip: Do not plan around an ekiben in Ise-Shima. Buy shio-musubi and fruit at the Iseshi platform FamilyMart before you board — that is the ekiben here.

sections.verdict: Ise is a mochi town, which is genuinely good news: most of the famous approach sweets are rice, bean and sugar. The clean win is Iwatoya's 生姜糖 (two ingredients, allergen-free by the maker's own list); the traps are Toba's shell-shaped madeleine and anything with 伊勢うどん or 佃煮 on the box.
sections.where: 赤福 kiosks at 伊勢市駅 (07:00–17:30), 宇治山田駅 (06:00–18:00) and 外宮前店 (09:00–17:00); 岩戸屋 at 内宮前 (09:00–17:00, daily); へんばや商店 伊勢市駅前店, 3 min from Iseshi Stn (09:00–17:00, closed Mon); 鳥羽1番街 and 珍海堂 at Toba Station (09:30–17:30/18:00, closed Thu).

rows.t: 生姜糖 (岩戸屋, 内宮前)
rows.note: Two ingredients — 砂糖（国内製造）and 生姜 — and the maker lists アレルゲン使用なし. The most reliably GF+vegan gift in Ise, and it keeps. Iwatoya also makes wheat items (伊勢うどんかりんとう, かりんとうお多福饅頭) on the premises, so a strict celiac should still read the box.

Rice, azuki and sugar with only 大豆 declared and no wheat — but no wheat-free-facility claim, and the same maker runs a barley line. Shelf life is effectively same-day, so treat it as a train snack, not a gift to carry home.

rows.t: 朔日餅 — June's 麦手餅 (1st of the month only)
rows.note: Do NOT assume the monthly Akafuku mochi is wheat-free. June's 麦手餅 is built on 麦こがし and もち麦粉 — barley, a gluten grain — alongside 砂糖, もち米粉, 小豆, 加工黒糖 and 米油. Plant-based, but out for a celiac.

rows.t: へんば餅 (へんばや商店 伊勢市駅前店)
rows.note: Griddle-marked mochi around koshi-an — rice and bean by construction, and the closest thing to a safe sweet within walking distance of the gates. But へんばや publishes no ingredient or allergen list online, so this is a read-the-box check. 2-day shelf life.

rows.t: 岩戸餅 / 二軒茶屋餅 (kinako mochi with koshi-an)
rows.note: Mochi rice, azuki koshi-an and kinako soy flour — no wheat by construction. Neither maker publishes a facility statement and Iwatoya runs wheat lines in the same shop, so read the label rather than assuming.

rows.t: シェル・レーヌ (ブランカ) — Toba's signature gift
rows.note: 粉糖・バター・卵白・小麦粉・アーモンド粉末 plus powdered pearl-shell calcium — wheat, dairy, egg AND an animal-derived mineral. The gift you will be handed in Toba, and a clean no on both counts.

rows.t: 伊勢うどん gift packs (every kiosk, both cities)
rows.note: The most likely thing to be pressed on you: wheat noodles plus a sachet of tamari-soy, bonito-dashi tare. Refuse it politely on both counts.

rows.t: 佃煮・かきしぐれ・真珠漬 (珍海堂, Toba Stn) and fish-cake gift boxes
rows.note: Toba's seafood gift wall is shellfish and fish simmered in wheat-brewed soy, or surimi fried in wheat batter — the whole aisle is out.

sections.tip: Hero buy: 生姜糖 from Iwatoya at Naiku-mae — sugar and ginger, nothing else, and the only Ise gift you can hand a celiac vegan without a caveat. Pair it with 赤福餅 for the train if you will eat it the same day.

playbook.tight: Toba: the FamilyMart on the overhead concourse outside the gates (06:00–20:00) is the only shop in the building and there is nothing inside the gates — shio-musubi, fruit, plain nuts and unsweetened soymilk, eat on board. Iseshi is genuinely easier: the FamilyMart sits on Kintetsu platform 4 INSIDE the gates (06:00–20:00), with a 24-hour FamilyMart 180 m out the north side if you land late.
playbook.gf: Assume every Ise/Toba speciality is wheat: Ise udon is wheat noodles in a tamari-soy tare (ふくすけ says so in writing and sends celiacs away), tekone-zushi is soy-marinated, grilled shellfish gets a soy brush, and even the 塩ふき昆布 beside a bowl of 赤福ぜんざい declares 小麦. Live on konbini shio-musubi, fruit and Iwatoya 生姜糖; 赤福餅 declares no wheat but makes no facility claim and the June 朔日餅 is barley. The only curated stops are Yamada Sanpou at Iseshi Station front (single-source claim — phone 070-8978-0276 first) and Chaya Ukanomitama out at Futami. Nothing here is celiac-certified.
playbook.vegan: Hidden katsuo/bonito dashi is the whole game — it is in the Ise udon tare (ふくすけ's own sheet names mackerel and bonito), in tekone-zushi and in most simmered sides. Reliable picks are shio-musubi, fruit, edamame, unsweetened soymilk, 赤福餅 and 生姜糖. ふくすけ will serve the udon without tare and give you salt, and Chaya Ukanomitama can modify items — ask both. Always ask 'dashi wa sakana?'

tokyo.name: Tokyo Station 東京駅
tokyo.intro: Japan's biggest station food complex, and for a celiac it is mostly a wall of wheat: GRANSTA's own shop directory returns ZERO results for グルテンフリー, and none of the 150+ ekiben is gluten-free or vegan. What you do get in-gate is one genuinely allergen-controlled sweet (the 米粉ろおる rice-flour roll) plus konbini rice and the B1 銀の鈴 wagashi counters — everything that resembles a real GF or vegan meal is a few minutes OUTSIDE the gates on the Yaesu/B1 side. Note the August 2026 change: T's たんたん, the vegan ramen anchor, moved out of the paid area.

sections.h: Tight transfer? Grab & go near the gates
sections.verdict: In-gate you are assembling a meal from single-ingredient konbini parts — plus one real find: a frozen rice-flour roll cake made on a dedicated allergen-free line, sold at the Shinkansen transfer gate.
sections.where: NewDays / NewDays KIOSK inside the gates (1F Central & North corridors, Keiyo Street, B1 Marunouchi-zaka, plus platform kiosks on Shinkansen tracks 20–23, roughly 6:30–21:30); 紀ノ国屋アントレ グランスタ東京 (1F North corridor, in-gate, 7:00–23:00 / Sun to 22:00); 駅弁屋 祭 セレクト at the Shinkansen south transfer gate.

rows.t: 米粉ろおる / TOIRO rice-flour roll (frozen, ¥450)
rows.note: The one allergen-controlled item inside the gates: 100% Uonuma-Koshihikari rice flour + soy cream, made on a dedicated line that never brings in the 8 mandatory allergens (wheat, egg, dairy…) with per-lot ppm testing (maker + JRE Media + OMOTENASHI Selection 2026 gold). Buy it at 駅弁屋 祭 セレクト 新幹線南乗換口 or the frozen vending machines on Shinkansen platforms 20–21. Egg/dairy-free with soy cream so likely vegan, but no vegan certification — read the label.

rows.t: Shio-musubi 塩むすび (plain salt onigiri, NewDays)
rows.note: The universal train move and the only rice ball documented broth-free at the major chains — but filled onigiri hide wheat soy sauce and bonito, and even 'plain' rice can be vinegared or dashi-cooked. Scan the label for 小麦; buy salt-only.

rows.t: Whole/cut fruit, plain nuts, edamame, unsweetened soymilk 無調整豆乳
rows.note: Single-ingredient items are the fastest reliable grab for both diets; skip flavoured/coated nuts and 調整豆乳, and take salads undressed (dressings are almost never GF).

rows.t: 紀ノ国屋アントレ グランスタ東京 (in-gate grocer-deli)
rows.note: The only real food shop inside the gates beyond konbini — own-baked bread and charcuterie (both out), but packaged goods, drinks and deli items you can label-scan. It is 1F by the Yaesu North gate, NOT the bigger B1 Marunouchi branch (that one is outside the gates).

rows.t: いろり庵きらく / in-gate stand-up soba — AVOID
rows.note: Station soba is wheat-blended, boiled in shared water, and the tsuyu is bonito dashi + wheat soy sauce; the tempura on top is wheat batter. Fast and cheap, and off-limits for both diets.

sections.tip: Under ~15 minutes: NewDays salt onigiri + fruit + soymilk, and if you are passing the Shinkansen south transfer gate, add a 米粉ろおる — it is the only thing in the paid area with a real allergen protocol behind it.

sections.verdict: Nothing inside the gates is GF or vegan — as of 1 Aug 2026 even T's たんたん moved OUT of the paid area. Everything below is a short walk on the Yaesu/B1 side, so only attempt it if you can leave the gates and come back.
sections.where: GRANSTA Tokyo B1 Square Zero (right out of the GRANSTA B1 north gate); Tokyo Ramen Street, B1 of Tokyo Station Ichibangai (Yaesu side, outside the gates); GRANSTA 八重北 1F 八重北食堂 (outside, Yaesu north — this is the lane that replaced the old Kitchen Street).

rows.t: T's たんたん (B1 Square Zero) — MOVED outside the gates
rows.note: 100% vegan kitchen — no meat, fish, dairy or egg anywhere, so no hidden bonito dashi; the landmark plant-based tantanmen plus vegan gyoza. NOT gluten-free: wheat 中華麺 and soy-sauce tare. It left the in-gate Keiyo Street spot on 31 Jul 2026 and reopened 1 Aug 2026 outside the gates (JR-Cross release) — old guides still say in-gate.

rows.t: そらのいろ NIPPON (Tokyo Ramen Street)
rows.note: The most useful shop here for both diets, and still an ask for each. A real グルテンフリー塩ラーメン uses brown-rice noodles boiled in a separate pot — but the shop's own page says contamination is possible, and that bowl's broth is chicken, so it is not vegan. Separately there is a genuine ヴィーガン担々麺 and vegan rice-flour water gyoza. Order the labelled bowl by name; the mushroom veg-soba is only vegan without the chicken chāshū and mushroom oil.

rows.t: Bangera's Spice Bistro & Cafe (グランスタ八重北 1F)
rows.note: Indian bistro whose menu marks vegetarian/vegan dishes with a leaf and flags gluten-free items — veg biryani, dosa, chickpea salad and a soy-meat 'chili con carne' are plant-based (own site + vegan blogs). Shared kitchen with naan/roti, ghee and seafood, so GF stays an ask: confirm the dish and the wheat handling at the table.

rows.t: KITADE TACOS (グランスタ東京 B1, in-gate)
rows.note: Tortillas are 100% Hokkaido corn, made at their own factory — structurally wheat-free, which is rare inside the gates. But the shop makes NO gluten-free claim, fillings are chicken tinga / pork carnitas / beef with unpublished sauces, and there is no vegan taco listed. Worth asking about; do not assume.

rows.t: The rest of Tokyo Ramen Street & the 八重北 izakaya floors
rows.note: Rokurinsha, Ikaruga, Hirugao and the other tsukemen/ramen counters are wheat noodles in pork/fish broth; 黒塀横丁 (B1) and 北町酒場 (2F) are yakitori, tempura, tonkatsu, gyoza and soba — wheat and dashi throughout.

sections.tip: If you need an actual meal, budget the time to exit the gates on the Yaesu side: T's たんたん for a guaranteed vegan bowl, そらのいろ NIPPON if you want the GF rice-noodle ramen and can accept a shared kitchen.

sections.verdict: Blunt version: there is no gluten-free ekiben and no vegan ekiben at Tokyo Station. 150+ varieties at 駅弁屋 祭 alone, and every one of them runs on wheat soy sauce, dashi, batter, egg or meat. The one vegan ekiben ever sold here (日本ばし大増 菜食弁当) was discontinued in 2020.
sections.where: 駅弁屋 祭 グランスタ東京 (1F Central Passage, in-gate, 5:30–22:00); 駅弁屋 踊 (1F in-gate, ~6:00–21:00); 駅弁屋 祭 セレクト 新幹線南乗換口 (in-gate, ~6:00–21:00); 崎陽軒 グランスタ東京 (B1, in-gate); Daimaru Tokyo B1 bento street (outside the gates, 10:00–20:00).

rows.t: 牛肉どまん中 (Yonezawa beef, the perennial #1)
rows.note: Beef simmered in a sweet-salty shoyu tare; the label declares 小麦 outright. Not GF, not vegan.

rows.t: 崎陽軒 シウマイ弁当
rows.note: Shumai wrappers are wheat flour, plus fried fish, anago, kamaboko and 厚焼卵 — wheat and animal in nearly every compartment.
Karaage in wheat batter, seasoned tomato rice, scrambled egg and smoked cheese — a triple no.

rows.t: 深川めし / 東京弁当 (Tokyo box)
rows.note: Clams, tamagoyaki, tsukudani, kasuzuke fish and simmered sides — soy sauce and dashi throughout. (Amusing footnote: the 東京弁当's dessert is a Funawa imo-yokan, the one GF/vegan-plausible thing in the box.)

rows.t: Allergen info at the ekiben counters
